title: Bukit Bintang Food: Jalan Alor, Lot 10 and Pavilion
metaDescription: Bukit Bintang food from street stalls to hotel dining: Jalan Alor at night, Lot 10 Hutong, Japanese food at Lot 10, Pavilion, and vegan options nearby.

contentBlocks.content: Bukit Bintang food covers every budget within a few streets. Jalan Alor is the street food lane, busiest after dark. Lot 10 has a hawker food hall in the basement and Japanese restaurants on the top floor. Pavilion Kuala Lumpur has restaurants on several levels. Around them you will find vegan kitchens, hotel dining and a bar on Level 59. This guide takes you through each, with the places from the Teeko restaurant directory and how to reach them from KLIA2.
Key Takeaways
Where do I go for street food? Jalan Alor. It is lined with seafood restaurants, hawker stalls and coffee shops, and it is busiest at night (Tourism Malaysia).
Is Jalan Alor halal? It is mixed. Some stalls serve pork and some do not, so check each stall before you order.
Where can I eat in air conditioning? Lot 10 Hutong in the basement of Lot 10, the Japanese restaurants on the top floor of Lot 10, and the food floors of Pavilion.
Is there pork-free ramen? Yes. TORIGEN at Lot 10 serves chicken broth ramen with no pork, no lard and no alcohol. It describes itself as pork-free, not halal certified.
How do I get here from KLIA2? Take the bus to Lalaport BBCC, two Monorail stops from Bukit Bintang, or see the KLIA2 to Bukit Bintang guide for every option.
Jalan Alor: street food after dark

Tourism Malaysia describes Jalan Alor as a street of seafood restaurants, hawker stalls and coffee shops serving Malaysian and international food, with the grills and woks firing once night falls (Tourism Malaysia). Expect satay, grilled seafood, chicken wings, beef skewers, noodles and fried snacks from open air stalls.
For grilled seafood off an open flame, Meng Kee Grill Fish is on Jalan Alor itself. Its menu leans on seafood and grilled dishes, and it suits a late meal with cold drinks.
Walk the whole street once before you sit down, and ask each stall about pork if it matters to you. Still hungry at midnight? The supper in Kuala Lumpur guide lists more late spots.
Lot 10: hawker stalls downstairs, Japanese upstairs

Lot 10 Shopping Centre is at 50 Jalan Sultan Ismail. Its basement holds Lot 10 Hutong, a food hall that brings well known KL hawker stalls under one roof (Tourism Malaysia). Lot 10's own website links to Lot 10 Hutong's delivery listing, which is labelled non-halal (Lot 10).

The top floor is J's Gate Dining, a floor of Japanese restaurants. Two of them are in the Teeko directory. TORIGEN Chicken Ramen serves a rich chicken broth ramen created by its Japanese owner, with no pork, no lard and no alcohol.
Kuro Ramen, on the same floor, serves tonkotsu ramen made with pork broth. Its Japanese owner, Akira Nagata, developed the recipe with a ramen master.
Take the escalators to the top floor for ramen, or head to the basement for hawker food.
Pavilion Kuala Lumpur: food on several floors

Pavilion's F&B directory lists restaurants on Level 1 in the Gourmet Emporium, on Levels 3 and 4 in the Connection, on Level 6 including Tokyo Street, and on Levels 8 and 9 in Pavilion Elite (Pavilion Kuala Lumpur). Check the directory for the outlet you want before you go; the mall is large.

Kampachi Pavilion is on Level 6. It was the first Kampachi outside the Equatorial Hotel, and it serves Japanese food from a team of Japanese chefs, with ingredients sourced from Japan, including seafood from Toyosu Market in Tokyo.
Open the card for its address and directions before you plan a dinner there.
Vegan and plant-based near Bukit Bintang
Kusa Japanese Vegan Restaurant serves Japanese vegan food at 2 Lorong Ceylon, a walk from Bukit Bintang Monorail station.

Minf Hauze Vegan Cafe is fully plant-based and cooks with no garlic, onion, egg, dairy, MSG, honey or alcohol. It is on the 3rd floor of the Cosway Building, 88 Jalan Raja Chulan, a few minutes' walk from Raja Chulan Monorail station.
See the vegan restaurant guide for Kuala Lumpur for more plant-based places across the city.
Dinner for an occasion
Li Yen is a Chinese restaurant in The Ritz-Carlton on Jalan Imbi. It has served Chinese classics for more than 20 years, with a menu by Executive Chinese Chef Alex Au that changes with the seasons.
Sushi Oribe is an omakase restaurant on Jalan Kia Peng, open since 2014. Chef Naoya Kawasaki serves a seasonal menu with ingredients flown in from Japan every week.
Open each card for the address and directions, and check how to reserve before you fly.
A drink with a view
Vertigo is a bar on Level 59 at 2 Jalan Conlay, with views over Kuala Lumpur. It serves cocktails made to order and Southeast Asian tapas, with a DJ.

For a street of bars, walk to Changkat Bukit Bintang, which Tourism Malaysia describes as a lively strip of lounges, bars and clubs, many with live music (Tourism Malaysia). See the KL bars guide for more.
Getting to Bukit Bintang from KLIA2

The bus from KLIA2 to Lalaport BBCC ends at an indoor hub in Bukit Bintang City Centre, open 24 hours. From there, the Monorail runs two stops, through Imbi, to Bukit Bintang. The bus to Pudu Sentral ends near Merdeka MRT, one stop from Pavilion Kuala Lumpur Bukit Bintang station. A fixed price taxi takes you from the arrival hall to your hotel in 45 to 60 minutes. The KLIA2 to Bukit Bintang guide compares all four.

content.heading: Land at KLIA2, eat in Bukit Bintang
content.subheading: Book the bus from KLIA2 to Lalaport BBCC and get off indoors, two Monorail stops from Bukit Bintang.

contentBlocks.content: Staying near Chinatown instead? Book the bus from KLIA2 to Pudu Sentral, listed on ttklia.com as KL City Centre (Pudu Sentral).
Frequently Asked Questions
Is Jalan Alor food halal?
Jalan Alor food is a mix of halal and non-halal. Stalls and restaurants each set their own menus, so ask at each one before you order.
Is there a food court in Bukit Bintang?
Yes. There is a food court in Bukit Bintang at Lot 10 Hutong, in the basement of Lot 10 Shopping Centre. Pavilion Kuala Lumpur also lists restaurants in its Gourmet Emporium on Level 1.
Where can I eat pork-free ramen in Bukit Bintang?
You can eat pork-free ramen in Bukit Bintang at TORIGEN Chicken Ramen, on the top floor of Lot 10. It uses chicken broth with no pork, no lard and no alcohol. It is not described as halal certified.
When is Jalan Alor busiest?
Jalan Alor is busiest at night, when the stalls fire up their grills and the tables fill the street. Go after dark for the full street.
How do I get to Bukit Bintang from KL Sentral?
To get to Bukit Bintang from KL Sentral, take the KL Monorail from the station in NU Sentral and ride five stops to Bukit Bintang.
Conclusion

Bukit Bintang food runs from Jalan Alor's stalls at night to the hawker hall under Lot 10, the Japanese floor above it, Pavilion's restaurants and a handful of vegan and hotel kitchens nearby. Pick the street for the atmosphere and the malls for air conditioning. Landing with a family or heavy bags? Book a fixed price taxi from KLIA2 to Bukit Bintang on ttklia.com and go straight to dinner.
